    ...
```

test_state_machine.py does it correctly:
```python
# At module top-level (line 38):
from conftest import _advance_to, _make_state
```

## Why It Matters

This was an IMPORTANT finding (aura-plugins-g5xp) in the original review. The FOLLOWUP implementation fixed inline imports in contract tests (test_aura_types.py) but did not apply the same fix in the newly introduced test_protocol_combinatorial.py. The same pattern recurs in new code.

Inline imports within test methods:
1. Obscure the test's dependencies — readers must scan each method body to understand what helpers are used
2. Incur a (tiny) import lookup cost on every parametrized invocation (up to 6 times × N parametrized cases)
3. Are inconsistent with the module-level import style used in test_state_machine.py and test_fixture_loader.py

## Fix

Move all 6 inline `from conftest import _advance_to` to the module top-level import block alongside the existing top-level imports (lines 29-50 of test_protocol_combinatorial.py).

TestP9SliceFailFastPattern (test_workflow.py:1160) tests the raw asyncio.wait(FIRST_EXCEPTION) semantic directly using plain asyncio coroutines:

```python
class TestP9SliceFailFastPattern:
    """Tests the asyncio pattern that the P9 supervisor uses to run parallel slices
    and cancel remaining slices on first failure. This tests the PATTERN — not an
    actual P9 Temporal workflow..."""

    async def test_first_exception_returns_on_first_failure(self) -> None:
        async def fast_fail() -> None:
            raise RuntimeError("Slice 0 failed with BLOCKER")

        async def long_slice() -> None:
            await asyncio.sleep(100)

        tasks = [
            asyncio.create_task(fast_fail(), name="fast-fail"),
            asyncio.create_task(long_slice(), name="long-slice"),
        ]
        done, pending = await asyncio.wait(tasks, return_when=asyncio.FIRST_EXCEPTION)
        ...
```

The test class docstring explicitly acknowledges it tests the "PATTERN — not an actual P9 Temporal workflow".

The production method EpochWorkflow._run_p9_slices() (workflow.py:454) wraps child workflow handles, not plain asyncio.Tasks. While ChildWorkflowHandle is awaitable, the actual integration (start_child_workflow, then asyncio.wait on handles) is untested.

## Why It Matters

The fail-fast semantic is a correctness requirement from the URD (aura-plugins-cz2t description: "asyncio.gather NEVER used — only workflow.wait()"). Testing only the raw pattern misses a production code path: that start_child_workflow handles behave as asyncio-awaitable tasks when passed to asyncio.wait. A subtle Temporal SDK behavior change could break this without test failure.

The existing sandbox tests (TestWorkflowEnvironmentSandbox) are skipped because they require a running Temporal server (4 skipped). There is no path that exercises _run_p9_slices() end-to-end in CI.

## What Would Be Better

A structural test that calls _run_p9_slices() with SliceInput lists and verifies the fail-fast pattern via the actual method, using a DI-friendly stub for SliceWorkflow (per R12 docstring pattern), without requiring a Temporal server.

Alternatively, the existing pattern tests are acceptable as a first-pass and the gap is documented. The tests that do exist (structural invariants, signal logic) are well-written.

## Not a Blocker Because

- The production code is correct per code inspection
- The asyncio pattern tests verify the control-flow semantics

{"id":"aura-plugins-cz2t","title":"IMPLEMENT: SliceWorkflow + ReviewPhaseWorkflow child workflow classes (fail-fast P9_SLICE)","description":"The supervisor implemented EpochWorkflow correctly but did not implement the two child workflow classes required by the ratified PROPOSAL-11 design.

## Critical Gap
workflow.py contains only EpochWorkflow. The following child workflow classes are entirely absent:
- SliceWorkflow: Represents a single P9_SLICE; runs concurrently with other SliceWorkflows
- ReviewPhaseWorkflow: Represents P10_CODE_REVIEW for a slice; receives ReviewAxis votes via signals

## Requirements (from PROPOSAL-11 / HANDOFF aura-plugins-6zro)

### SliceWorkflow
- @workflow.defn class
- Accepts SliceInput (dataclass with epoch_id, slice_id, phase_spec: SerializablePhaseSpec)
- Executes slice activities (or stubs with R12 docstrings for now)
- Returns SliceResult (or PhaseResult)
- Fail-fast: EpochWorkflow must use workflow.wait(slice_handles, return_when=FIRST_EXCEPTION)
  and cancel remaining handles on first exception

### ReviewPhaseWorkflow
- @workflow.defn class
- Accepts ReviewInput (dataclass)
- @workflow.signal handler for ReviewVoteSignal (axis: ReviewAxis)
- wait_condition until all 3 ReviewAxis members have voted (using ReviewAxis enum members)
- try/except ApplicationError around child_handle.signal() calls (race protection)
- Returns PhaseResult with vote_result

### EpochWorkflow Integration
- P9_SLICE: start N SliceWorkflow children, then workflow.wait(handles, return_when=FIRST_EXCEPTION)
  On first exception: cancel pending handles, propagate
- P10_CODE_REVIEW: start ReviewPhaseWorkflow children; wait for completion

## Acceptance Criteria
- SliceWorkflow class exists with @workflow.defn
- ReviewPhaseWorkflow class exists with @workflow.defn + @workflow.signal for ReviewVoteSignal
- EpochWorkflow.p9_slice_phase() uses workflow.wait(FIRST_EXCEPTION) + cancel-on-failure
- EpochWorkflow.p10_review_phase() starts ReviewPhaseWorkflow child(ren) and waits
- asyncio.gather NEVER used — only workflow.wait()
- Tests: fail-fast behavior verified; signal routing verified
- No regressions in existing tests","status":"open","priority":2,"issue_type":"task","owner":"dayvidpham@gmail.com","created_at":"2026-02-26T20:53:52Z","created_by":"David Huu Pham","updated_at":"2026-02-26T23:39:16Z"}

{"id":"aura-plugins-oyxw","title":"FIX: query_audit_events drops role filter — add role: RoleId | None to activity","description":"The query_audit_events activity (audit_activities.py) does not forward the role parameter to AuditTrail.query_events even though the Protocol interface supports it.

## Gap
In audit_activities.py:
- Activity signature is: query_audit_events(epoch_id: str, phase: PhaseId | None = None)
- Missing: role: RoleId | None = None parameter
- The delegation call: await _AUDIT_TRAIL.query_events(epoch_id=epoch_id, phase=phase)
- Missing: role=role kwarg

The AuditTrail Protocol defines:
  async def query_events(self, *, epoch_id: str | None = None, phase: PhaseId | None = None, role: RoleId | None = None) -> list[AuditEvent]

## Fix Required
1. Add role: RoleId | None = None to query_audit_events signature
2. Forward role=role in the _AUDIT_TRAIL.query_events() call
3. Update any callers and tests accordingly

## Rationale
Without the role filter, queries that scope to a specific agent role (e.g. 'show only SUPERVISOR audit events for this epoch') silently return unfiltered results. This is a silent correctness failure.

## Acceptance Criteria
- query_audit_events activity accepts role: RoleId | None = None
- Delegation call passes role=role to _AUDIT_TRAIL.query_events()
- Test: query_audit_events with role filter returns only role-matching events
- No regressions in existing tests","status":"open","priority":2,"issue_type":"task","owner":"dayvidpham@gmail.com","created_at":"2026-02-26T20:53:36Z","created_by":"David Huu Pham","updated_at":"2026-02-26T23:39:16Z"}

{"id":"aura-plugins-txgq","title":"FIX: EpochState.review_votes key type — dict[str, VoteType] → dict[ReviewAxis, VoteType]","description":"EpochState.review_votes is typed as dict[str, VoteType] but should be dict[ReviewAxis, VoteType] to maintain type coherence with ReviewAxis(StrEnum) and ReviewVoteSignal.axis: ReviewAxis.

## Gap (workflow.py)
  @dataclass
  class EpochState:
      ...
      review_votes: dict[str, VoteType] = field(default_factory=dict)

Should be:
  review_votes: dict[ReviewAxis, VoteType] = field(default_factory=dict)

## Why This Matters
PROPOSAL-9 introduced ReviewAxis(StrEnum) specifically to replace raw str keys in vote tracking.
PROPOSAL-10 fixed ReviewVoteSignal.axis: str → ReviewAxis.
But EpochState.review_votes still uses str as key, defeating the type safety fix.

Because ReviewAxis is a StrEnum, dict[ReviewAxis, VoteType] is backward-compatible at runtime
(StrEnum values are strings), but mypy/pyright will catch misuse at development time.

## Fix Required
1. Change review_votes: dict[str, VoteType] → dict[ReviewAxis, VoteType] in EpochState
2. Update all dict assignments: self._state.review_votes[signal.axis] = signal.vote
   (signal.axis is already ReviewAxis, so no cast needed)
3. Update tests to use ReviewAxis.CORRECTNESS etc. as keys

## Acceptance Criteria
- EpochState.review_votes: dict[ReviewAxis, VoteType]
- All assignments use ReviewAxis enum members as keys
- Tests verify ReviewAxis keys (not raw strings)
- No regressions","status":"open","priority":2,"issue_type":"task","owner":"dayvidpham@gmail.com","created_at":"2026-02-26T20:54:03Z","created_by":"David Huu Pham","updated_at":"2026-02-26T23:39:16Z"}

### Round 1 Finding Resolution

#### BLOCKER (A+B): C-blocker-dual-parent kwarg fixed

Round 1 found: violation_args used followup_slice_id but method signature has slice_id.

PROPOSAL-2 YAML:
  violation_args: { blocker_task_id: "leaf-1", severity_group_id: "", slice_id: "slice-1" }

Actual signature (constraints.py:782-786):
  def check_blocker_dual_parent(self, blocker_task_id: str, severity_group_id: str, slice_id: str)

**VERIFIED CORRECT.** All three kwargs match. Empty severity_group_id triggers the expected violation.

#### Structural (C): Removed _coerce_violation_args

Replaced with single inline coercion in fixture loader:
  if "phase" in raw_args and isinstance(raw_args["phase"], str):
      raw_args["phase"] = PhaseId(raw_args["phase"])

**VERIFIED CORRECT.** See PhaseId coercion sufficiency analysis below.

#### Structural (C): Removed _factory — audit constraints use violation_state with transition_history

C-audit-never-delete and C-audit-dep-chain now use violation_state YAML (the existing code path), extended with optional transition_history list. No separate _factory dispatch mechanism.

Each entry verified against actual method signatures in constraints.py.

   Signature: (self, blocker_task_id: str, severity_group_id: str, slice_id: str) — CORRECT

**Result: All 20 violation_method + violation_args entries match their method signatures exactly. Zero kwarg mismatches.**

---

### Verification 2: Audit Constraint transition_history Extension

**C-audit-never-delete:**
YAML: violation_state with current_phase: p2, no transition_history key.
Fixture loader: transition_history defaults to empty list in EpochState (default_factory=list).
check_audit_trail (line 664-668): state.current_phase != P1_REQUEST and not state.transition_history -> fires C-audit-never-delete.
**CORRECT.** P2 with empty history fires the expected violation.

**C-audit-dep-chain:**
YAML: violation_state with current_phase: p2, transition_history containing one record with triggered_by: "".
Fixture loader: constructs TransitionRecord(from_phase=PhaseId("p1"), to_phase=PhaseId("p2"), triggered_by="", condition_met="classification confirmed", timestamp=datetime.now(tz=timezone.utc)).
TransitionRecord dataclass (state_machine.py:56-74): has fields from_phase, to_phase, timestamp, triggered_by, condition_met, success=True. All provided. success defaults to True (correct for a valid transition).
check_audit_trail (line 685-701): iterates records, checks if not record.triggered_by — empty string is falsy, fires C-audit-dep-chain.
Isolation: transition_history is non-empty (one record), so C-audit-never-delete does NOT co-fire.
**CORRECT.** Both constraints independently testable without co-firing.

The post-construction approach state.transition_history.extend(transition_history) is correct because EpochState.transition_history uses field(default_factory=list) — a mutable list.

---

### Verification 3: PhaseId Coercion Sufficiency

The single inline coercion handles phase: str -> PhaseId. Scanning all 20 violation_args entries:

- C-supervisor-cartographers: phase="p8" -> PhaseId.P8_IMPL_PLAN — NEEDS coercion, COVERED
- All other entries: str, bool, int, list[str] only — natively handled by YAML parsing

No other violation_method takes PhaseId in its args. (check_state and check_transition take PhaseId but route through different dispatch paths, not violation_method.)

**CORRECT.** PhaseId coercion for check_supervisor_cartographers is the only needed coercion.

---

### NOTE: C-worker-gates Duplicate Key Concern

The proposal lists C-worker-gates in the "15 constraints — use check_structural as violation_method" group. However, C-worker-gates is NOT one of the 21 skipped constraints — it is one of the 5 existing RUNNABLE constraints (protocol.yaml line 704-712, uses violation_state with blocker_count: 1 at p10, testing check_blocker_gate).

If the implementer adds a second C-worker-gates entry with violation_method: check_worker_gates, YAML will silently overwrite the first — losing the blocker_count state-based test. The correct count for the structural group should be 14, not 15. The proposal's validation checklist claims "5 existing runnable constraint tests still pass" but including C-worker-gates in the new entries would replace one of those 5.

This is NOT a BLOCKER because:
- Both check_blocker_gate and check_worker_gates emit constraint_id="C-worker-gates", so the test assertion still passes
- The blocker_count behavior is tested elsewhere (transition tests, check_transition)
- The implementer will likely notice the YAML duplicate during implementation

However, for the proposal to be internally consistent: the structural group should list 14 entries (removing C-worker-gates), and the total new entries should be 2 audit + 14 structural + 4 naming = 20 (matching the 20 un-skipped from 21).

### End-User Alignment

1. **End-users:** Developers running the test suite
2. **What they want:** All tests pass, no false skips, reliable CI

5. **MVP scope:** Appropriate — test infrastructure only, no production code changes
6. **Validation checklist:** Complete and verifiable, with the C-worker-gates counting note above

## VOTE: ACCEPT

All four correctness verification items pass:

1. C-blocker-dual-parent kwarg fix: slice_id matches method signature exactly — VERIFIED
2. All 20 violation_method + violation_args entries: zero kwarg mismatches against actual method signatures — VERIFIED

4. PhaseId coercion: only needed for check_supervisor_cartographers(phase="p8"), correctly implemented — VERIFIED

The C-worker-gates counting note is an implementation-time discovery, not a design correctness issue. The Round 1 BLOCKER is resolved. The proposal is correct."}

### 1. `_check_tmux(search_path=...)` — Proportional, Not Over-Engineering

The proposed signature:

```python
def _check_tmux(search_path: str | None = None) -> bool:
    return shutil.which("tmux", path=search_path) is not None
```

This is **proportional** for three reasons:

1. **It forwards an existing stdlib parameter.** `shutil.which` already accepts a `path` keyword argument. The DI parameter is not an invented abstraction — it exposes a capability that already exists one layer down. The function remains a single expression.

2. **It follows the established codebase pattern.** `parse_args(argv)` accepts an explicit `argv` parameter for the same reason: testability without global state mutation. `resolve_connection(cli_args, env_dict, yaml_section)` uses the same pattern. The `search_path` parameter is consistent with both.

3. **The alternative is worse.** Without this parameter, the test must manipulate `os.environ["PATH"]` (global mutable state), which is a test isolation hazard — if the test crashes before restoring PATH, subsequent tests may fail in mysterious ways. Or the test must use `unittest.mock.patch`, which contradicts the project's no-mocking-framework pattern. The DI parameter is the cleanest option.

**Verdict:** Not over-engineering. One optional parameter on a private function. Zero cognitive overhead for callers who pass nothing.

### 2. Config Test Matrix — Clean DI, No New Abstractions

The 8-row test matrix passes explicit `cli_args`, `env_dict`, `yaml_section` dicts to `resolve_connection()`. This is the same DI-via-explicit-parameters pattern already established. No test fixtures, no config builders, no parameterized test abstractions beyond plain function calls with plain dicts.

The matrix is exhaustive without being redundant: 6 rows test all pairwise priority combinations (CLI>env, CLI>YAML, env>YAML, env>default, YAML>default, CLI>all), plus 2 error cases (missing file, malformed YAML). Pure field name correction. The `QueryStateResult.votes` external field name is preserved — only the internal reference changes from `state.votes` to `state.review_votes`. This decoupling (internal field name vs. external API name) is the right design choice. No elegance regression.

### 4. Correctness Fix 2 (Typed `query_events`) — Strictly Better

Changing `SqliteAuditTrail.query_events` from `phase: str = ""` to `phase: PhaseId | None = None` is an elegance improvement, not a regression. It enforces the project's "strongly-typed enums over stringly-typed API" principle. The implementation detail (`.value` for SQL WHERE clauses) is cleanly encapsulated inside the method. Callers pass enums; the method converts to strings only at the SQL boundary. This is the correct abstraction level.

The `None`-means-no-filter semantics is also cleaner than empty-string-means-no-filter. `None` has clear intent ("I did not specify this filter"). Empty string is ambiguous ("Did I forget to set it, or is empty string a valid filter value?").

(Reviewer A) and 5 test quality gaps (Reviewer B). Reviewer C accepted.

## Correctness Fix 1 (BLOCKER): `state.review_votes` not `state.votes`

**Source:** Reviewer A (aura-plugins-a20y6)

EpochState in `scripts/aura_protocol/state_machine.py:48` defines the field
as `review_votes`, not `votes`.

**Before (PROPOSAL-4):**
```python
@workflow.query
def full_state(self) -> QueryStateResult:
    state = self._sm.state
    return QueryStateResult(
        ...
        votes=dict(state.votes),  # WRONG: AttributeError
        ...
    )
```

**After (PROPOSAL-5):**
```python
@workflow.query
def full_state(self) -> QueryStateResult:
    state = self._sm.state
    return QueryStateResult(
        ...
        votes=dict(state.review_votes),  # FIXED: matches EpochState field name
        ...
    )
```

The `QueryStateResult` field remains named `votes` (cleaner API for CLI
consumers). Only the source reference changes.

## Correctness Fix 2 (IMPORTANT): SqliteAuditTrail query_events type signature

**Source:** Reviewer A (aura-plugins-a20y6)

The AuditTrail Protocol in `scripts/aura_protocol/interfaces.py:140-146`
defines `query_events` with typed parameters:

```python
async def query_events(
    self, *, epoch_id: str | None = None,
    phase: PhaseId | None = None,
    role: RoleId | None = None
) -> list[AuditEvent]: ...
```

**Before (PROPOSAL-4):**
```python
class SqliteAuditTrail:
    async def query_events(self, *, epoch_id: str = "",
                           phase: str = "", role: str = "") -> list[AuditEvent]:
```

**After (PROPOSAL-5):**
```python
class SqliteAuditTrail:
    async def query_events(
        self, *,
        epoch_id: str | None = None,
        phase: PhaseId | None = None,
        role: RoleId | None = None,
    ) -> list[AuditEvent]:
        """Query audit events with optional filters.

        Converts PhaseId/RoleId enums to their .value for SQL WHERE clauses.
        None parameters are omitted from the filter.
        """
        conditions: list[str] = []
        params: list[str] = []
        if epoch_id is not None:
            conditions.append("epoch_id = ?")
            params.append(epoch_id)
        if phase is not None:
            conditions.append("phase = ?")
            params.append(phase.value)
        if role is not None:
            conditions.append("role = ?")
            params.append(role.value)
        ...
```

This matches the Protocol signature exactly. Enum `.value` is used for SQL
string comparison. `None` means "no filter on this dimension."

## Test Quality Fix 1: `signal complete` BDD criteria

**Source:** Reviewer B (aura-plugins-zath7), item 1

**Added BDD criteria:**

**Given** `aura-msg signal complete --epoch-id E1 --slice-id S1 --output "done"` **when** slice workflow running **then** sends SliceCompleteSignal(slice_id="S1", success=True, output="done") **should not** send signal to non-existent workflow (exit 3)

**Given** `aura-msg signal complete --epoch-id E1 --slice-id S1 --error "failed"` **when** signaling failure **then** sends SliceCompleteSignal(slice_id="S1", success=False, error="failed") **should not** set success=True when error is provided

**Given** `aura-msg signal complete` without `--slice-id` **when** parsing **then** prints usage error, exits 1 **should not** send incomplete signal

## Test Quality Fix 3: Exit code BDD criteria

**Source:** Reviewer B (aura-plugins-zath7), item 3

**Added BDD criteria:**

**Given** Temporal server unreachable **when** `aura-msg query state --epoch-id E1` **then** prints "connection error: ..." to stderr, exits 2 **should not** exit 0 or raise unhandled exception

**Given** workflow not found **when** `aura-msg query state --epoch-id nonexistent` **then** prints "workflow error: workflow 'nonexistent' not found" to stderr, exits 3 **should not** print stack trace

**Given** `aura-msg epoch start --epoch-id E1` on already-running workflow **when** Temporal returns WorkflowAlreadyStartedError **then** prints "workflow error: epoch 'E1' already running" to stderr, exits 3 **should not** exit 0

Test implementation: subprocess-based integration tests (same pattern as
test_aurad.py `test_help_output`). For connection errors, pass a bogus
`--server-address localhost:1` to guarantee connection failure.

## Test Quality Fix 4: tmux detection test strategy

**Source:** Reviewer B (aura-plugins-zath7), item 4

The `_check_tmux()` function uses `shutil.which("tmux")`. Test strategy:

```python
# Test via subprocess with modified PATH (no mocking frameworks)
async def test_tmux_not_found():
    env = ActivityEnvironment()
    # Inject empty PATH so shutil.which finds nothing
    import os
    old_path = os.environ.get("PATH", "")
    os.environ["PATH"] = ""
    try:
        result = await env.run(execute_slice_command, "aura-swarm start ...", "s1", "e1")
        assert not result.success
        assert "tmux" in result.error
    finally:
        os.environ["PATH"] = old_path

async def test_tmux_found_command_runs():
    # Only run if tmux actually exists on test system
    if shutil.which("tmux") is None:
        pytest.skip("tmux not available")
    ...
```

Alternative (cleaner): make `_check_tmux` accept an optional `path` parameter
for testability without PATH manipulation:

```python
def _check_tmux(search_path: str | None = None) -> bool:
    return shutil.which("tmux", path=search_path) is not None
```

Then tests pass `search_path="/nonexistent"` or `search_path=<dir-with-mock-tmux>`.
This follows the existing DI pattern (no unittest.mock). Recommend the
`search_path` parameter approach.

## Test Quality Fix 5: Hook/shell script test boundary

**Source:** Reviewer B (aura-plugins-zath7), item 5

Test boundary for `hooks/scripts/session-register.sh`:

```python
# Test the shell script via subprocess with a mock aura-msg on PATH
async def test_session_register_hook():
    """Hook script calls aura-msg session register + query state."""
    # Create a mock aura-msg that records invocations
    mock_dir = tmp_path / "bin"
    mock_dir.mkdir()
    mock_script = mock_dir / "aura-msg"
    mock_script.write_text('#!/bin/sh\necho "$@" >> /tmp/aura-msg-calls.txt\n')
    mock_script.chmod(0o755)

    result = subprocess.run(
        ["bash", "hooks/scripts/session-register.sh"],
        env={
            "PATH": f"{mock_dir}:/usr/bin:/bin",
            "AURA_EPOCH_ID": "test-epoch",
            "CLAUDE_SESSION_ID": "test-session",
        },
        capture_output=True, text=True,
    )
    assert result.returncode == 0
    calls = Path("/tmp/aura-msg-calls.txt").read_text()
    assert "session register" in calls
    assert "query state" in calls

async def test_session_register_hook_no_epoch():
    """Hook script exits silently when AURA_EPOCH_ID is not set."""
    result = subprocess.run(
        ["bash", "hooks/scripts/session-register.sh"],
        env={"PATH": "/usr/bin:/bin"},  # no AURA_EPOCH_ID
        capture_output=True, text=True,
    )
    assert result.returncode == 0
    assert result.stdout == ""
```

The test boundary is the shell script itself, tested via subprocess with
controlled environment. No Temporal server needed for hook tests.

{"id":"aura-plugins-8xhrw","title":"PROPOSAL-1-REVIEW-C-1","description":"references:
  proposal: aura-plugins-4vypg
  urd: aura-plugins-jbnx3
  request: aura-plugins-pv2ek
---
## Review Axis: Elegance

**VOTE: ACCEPT**

### Summary

The proposal is structurally clean, idiomatically Go, and appropriately complex for the problem. The pkg/internal split is correct, naming conventions are consistent, and the interface surfaces are well-scoped. No over-engineering or unnecessary abstraction is present.

### Findings

**Strengths:**

1. **pkg/protocol vs internal/ split is correct.** Only true convergence types (`PhaseId`, `EventType`, `AuditEvent`, `SessionEntry`) are exported to `pkg/protocol`. Everything else stays internal. This mirrors the reference repo pattern (`pkg/schema` for shared types, `internal/` for implementation). The rule is clear and will hold as the codebase grows.

2. **Dependency injection via struct (T7) is idiomatic Go.** Replacing the Python global `AuditTrail` singleton with DI through constructors is the right call. The `Trail` interface is minimal — two methods — and testable with an in-memory implementation.

3. **Handler functions are CLI-framework-agnostic (T2/D4).** Standalone `func QueryState(ctx, conn, epochID, fmt) (int, error)` functions are testable in isolation. The Cobra `RunE` → handler dispatch pattern is the correct Go idiom (mirrored in the reference repo's `cmd_*.go` files).

4. **Signal/query constants in `internal/temporal/constants.go` (T3/D10).** Prevents name drift between pastured and pasture-msg. Compile-time safety. Simple and correct.

5. **`internal/types/` vs `pkg/protocol/` split.** Internal types (`PhaseId` in types, `PhaseId` in protocol) could be a naming collision concern, but the proposal clearly intends `pkg/protocol.PhaseId` as the canonical public type and `internal/types/` as supporting enums (`VoteType`, `ReviewAxis`, `Domain`, `RoleId`). This is clean.

6. **`StructuredError` (T8) implements `error` + `Report(io.Writer)`.** Testable via `bytes.Buffer`. Actionable fields (what/why/impact/fix). Not over-engineered — no reflection, no dynamic dispatch. Correct.

7. **`modernc.org/sqlite` (T4).** Pure Go, CGO_ENABLED=0 compatible. Appropriate for audit trail workload (low-volume writes, no high-throughput reads). The tradeoff is clearly documented and proportionate.

8. **Wave schedule is sound.** S1/S2/S3 as foundation, then parallel core, then integration. Wave 4 (pasture-release) correctly noted as independent. No false dependencies.

9. **Naming conventions are consistent.** `pasture-*` for Go binaries, `aura-*` for Python tools. Module path `github.com/dayvidpham/pasture` is clean (no vanity domain, no `/v2`). Aligns with D1/D2 in URD.

10. **`ParsePhaseId` supporting multiple formats** ("p1", "1", "request", "p1_request") is appropriate — agents may produce any of these and the parser is the right place to normalize.

**Minor observations (non-blocking):**

- `AuditTrail` string field in `PasturedConfig` uses `"memory" | "sqlite"` as raw strings. A typed `AuditTrailBackend` enum exists in `internal/types/config_types.go` — the config struct should use that type directly rather than `string`. The proposal has this enum defined but the config struct is stringly-typed. Not a blocker since it's an implementation detail, but worth noting for the implementation slices.

- `SemVer.Bump(kind string)` takes a string argument (`"major" | "minor" | "patch"`) rather than a typed enum. There is a `BumpKind` type opportunity here. Again, implementation detail — the interface defines what's needed.

- `internal/acp/` has both `Client` (struct) and `SessionHandler` (interface). The struct is not exported, which is correct for an internal package. However, `NewClient(handler SessionHandler) *Client` returning a concrete `*Client` from an internal package is fine since callers inside the same module will use it.

- The `Exec(cmd string, args ...string) error` on `PluginRegistry` is a shell-execution method on what is otherwise a data type. This is a slight mixing of concerns (registry as data model vs registry as command runner). Acceptable for MVP scope; could be refactored later into a separate `RegistryRunner` type.

**No blockers identified.**

The design complexity is proportional to the innate complexity of the problem (Temporal-backed multi-agent orchestration + ACP client + polyrepo release management). Nothing is added without purpose. The architecture aligns with the reference repo patterns where directly comparable (`pkg/schema` → `pkg/protocol`, `cmd/aura/cmd_*.go` → `cmd/pasture-msg/*.go`, `internal/config` → `internal/config`).","status":"open","priority":2,"issue_type":"task","owner":"dayvidpham@gmail.com","created_at":"2026-03-10T03:40:06Z","created_by":"David Huu Pham","updated_at":"2026-03-10T03:40:06Z"}

## Project Identity

Pasture is the Go successor to aura-protocol. The Python aura-* tools remain for codegen/protocol definition. Go binaries use the pasture-* naming convention.

- Repo: github.com/dayvidpham/pasture
- Go module: github.com/dayvidpham/pasture
- CLI binaries: pastured (worker daemon), pasture-msg (Temporal messaging), pasture-release (version/release management)

## Requirements

### R1: Port aurad → pastured
- Temporal worker daemon registering EpochWorkflow, SliceWorkflow, ReviewPhaseWorkflow
- 4 activities: check_constraints, record_transition, record_audit_event, query_audit_events
- Pluggable audit trail: InMemoryAuditTrail (dev) + SqliteAuditTrail (prod)
- Search attribute auto-registration (ensure_search_attributes) on startup
- Config resolution: CLI > env > YAML > defaults (Viper)
- Signal-driven state machine: advance_phase, submit_vote, slice_progress, register_session
- Pipeline pattern: PhaseId is a name-only string (e.g. "request", "elicit"); ordering determined by index in a Pipeline slice, not by the PhaseId value itself

### R2: Port aura-msg → pasture-msg
- All 8 subcommands: query state, epoch start/cancel/terminate, signal vote/complete, phase advance, session register
- Command pattern: Cobra RunE dispatch → standalone handler functions (testable without Cobra)
- Structured error reporting: ErrorCategory + report_error(what/why/impact/fix) → stderr
- Output formatting: JSON/text switch via OutputFormat enum
- Exit codes: 0=success, 1=validation, 2=connection, 3=workflow, 4=config

### R3: Port aura-release → pasture-release
- Version file auto-discovery (pyproject.toml, package.json, plugin.json, marketplace.json)
- SemVer parsing + bumping (major/minor/patch)
- Changelog generation from conventional commits
- Git commit + tag automation with rollback
- Plugin registry: init, add, list, remove
- NEW: registry exec (run command across all registered plugin repos)
- NEW: registry sync-versions (update marketplace.json from each plugin current version)
- NEW: registry release-order (topological sort for inter-plugin dependencies)

### R4: ACP Integration (Full Client)
- Locally defined ACP wire types aligned with ACP protocol spec (no external acp-go-sdk dependency)
- Shared types: ContentBlock, SessionUpdate, ToolCallUpdate, ToolKind, StopReason
- Shared indexer: []acp.SessionUpdate → []SessionEntry conversion
- Live ACP client: JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdio, receive SessionUpdate notifications
- Adapter interface with compile-time static registry (no runtime mutation, no mutex needed)
- Two provider adapters: Claude JSONL → ACP types, OpenCode JSON → ACP types
- Claude Code hooks interface: 12 hook events for lifecycle/error/session event capture

### R5: Shared Go Library
- Reusable internal/ packages: config, errors, types, temporal, formatters
- Shared signal/query name constants (prevent drift between pastured and pasture-msg)
- Type definitions portable to agent-data-leverage analytics pipeline (convergence path)

### R6: Build & Distribution (4 channels)
- Nix flake (primary): buildGoModule, Home Manager integration
- GitHub Releases: static binaries for linux-amd64, linux-arm64, darwin-amd64, darwin-arm64 (CGO_ENABLED=0)
- /pasture:install-cli skill: Claude Code skill for OS/arch detection + binary fetch
- go install: standard Go install path

### R7: Polyrepo Marketplace
- pasture repo is separate from aura-plugins (Python stays)
- pasture added as git submodule in aura-plugins
- Extend pasture-release with registry exec, sync-versions, release-order
- marketplace.json coordination between pasture and aura-plugins repos
- mani as complementary tool for non-release cross-repo operations (evaluate, not mandatory)

## Priorities (user-stated)

1. pastured + pasture-msg (core protocol orchestration) — MVP gate
2. ACP full client (live agent observability) — MVP gate
3. pasture-release (polyrepo management) — MVP gate
4. Shared Go library convergence with analytics — planned, not MVP gate
5. Web interface for live agent observation/interaction — end vision, not MVP

## Design Choices (from elicitation + UAT)

- D1: Go binaries rebrand to pasture-*, Python tools keep aura-* naming
- D2: Module path: github.com/dayvidpham/pasture (no vanity domain, no /v2)
- D3: Cobra + Viper for CLI + config (research confirmed, Temporal CLI uses same)
- D4: Hybrid Command pattern: Cobra RunE → standalone handlers (testable)
- D5: Reference agent-data-leverage Go patterns, plan convergence, do not modify that repo
- D6: Full ACP client in MVP (ambitious but high value per user)
- D7: Hooks interface for Claude Code integration — 12 hook events:
  - Lifecycle (7): phase_transition, vote_recorded, slice_started, slice_completed, epoch_started, epoch_completed, review_cycle
  - Error (3): slice_failed, constraint_violation, connection_lost
  - Session (2): session_started, session_ended
  - Configurable per-handler dispatch timeout via functional options (WithDispatchTimeout)
- D8: All 4 distribution channels in MVP (Nix, GitHub Releases, skill, go install)
- D9: Extend pasture-release (not replace) for polyrepo coordination
- D10: Shared signal/query constants to prevent name drift (research risk finding)
- D11: No internal/types/aliases.go — import pkg/protocol directly (UAT-1)
- D12: ACP Adapter interface with compile-time static registry, not standalone functions (UAT-1)
- D13: Keep mixed enum value styles — context-appropriate (e.g. PhaseId kebab-case, EventType PascalCase) (UAT-1)
- D14: Exit code 4 for CategoryConfig (Impl UAT-1)
- D15: pasture added as git submodule in aura-plugins (UAT-1)
- D16: Pipeline pattern — PhaseId = name-only string, index in Pipeline slice determines pX number (Impl UAT-1)

## MVP Goals

A first release of pasture that:
1. pastured connects to Temporal, registers all workflows/activities, handles signals/queries
2. pasture-msg sends all 8 commands to pastured via Temporal
3. ACP client connects to running Claude Code agents, receives live SessionUpdate stream via Adapter interface with static registry
4. pasture-release manages versions across polyrepo marketplace
5. All 4 distribution channels functional
6. Tests: unit + integration, Temporal test suite

## End-Vision Goals

- Multi-agent orchestration: any ACP-compatible agent (Claude Code, OpenCode, Gemini CLI, Copilot) participates in Pasture epochs
- Live observability platform: real-time dashboards showing agent sessions, cost tracking, quality metrics
- Web interface: observe and respond to live agent sessions through a browser
- Analytics convergence: pasture types feed into agent-data-leverage analytics pipeline
- Plugin marketplace backbone: hosting, versioning, distribution, analytics for Claude Code plugins"}

## Specification

Create hooks manager singleton (like auditTrail pattern) and wire hook dispatch into existing Temporal activities and workflows.

### Changes Required

1. **Hooks singleton** (internal/hooks/singleton.go — new file):
   - Module-level `var hooksMgr *Manager`
   - `InitHooksManager(mgr *Manager)` — called once before worker starts
   - `GetManager() *Manager` — returns singleton (nil-safe, returns no-op if uninitialized)
   - Follow same pattern as internal/temporal/activities.go auditTrail singleton

2. **DispatchHook activity** (internal/hooks/singleton.go):
   - `DispatchHook(ctx context.Context, payload HookPayload) error` — Temporal activity
   - Delegates to hooksMgr.Dispatch(ctx, payload)
   - Returns actionable error if hooksMgr is nil

3. **Hook dispatch in existing activities** (internal/temporal/activities.go):
   - RecordTransition: after recording, dispatch HookPhaseTransition with phase data
   - CheckConstraints: if violations found, dispatch HookConstraintViolation

4. **Hook dispatch in workflows** (internal/temporal/workflow_slice.go):
   - After slice start: execute DispatchHook activity with HookSliceStarted
   - After slice complete: execute DispatchHook activity with HookSliceCompleted
   - On slice failure: execute DispatchHook activity with HookSliceFailed
   - NOTE: Must use ExecuteActivity (not direct call) since workflows cannot have goroutines

5. **Register DispatchHook activity** in RegisterWorkflows()

- internal/hooks/singleton_test.go (new)

## Summary

UAT revisions from Phase 11 review. Three items:
1. Hybrid XML struct marshalling for schema.go (non-CDATA sections use encoding/xml)
2. Port validate_schema.py 3-layer validator to Go
3. Enhanced structural test fixtures (header-based, constraints-based, figure-based)

## Architecture

### Wave 1: Public Interfaces + Types (sequential, blocks everything)

**SLICE-A: XML schema types + validator interface**
- `internal/codegen/schema_types.go` — encoding/xml annotated structs for all 17 sections:
  - AuraProtocol (root), EnumSection, LabelSection, ReviewAxesSection, PhasesSection,
    RolesSection, CommandsSection, HandoffsSection, ConstraintsSection, TaskTitlesSection,
    DocumentsSection, DependencyModelSection, FollowupLifecycleSection,
    ProcedureStepsSection, ChecklistsSection, CoordinationCommandsSection,
    WorkflowsSection, FiguresSection
  - Each section struct has xml tags for marshalling
  - CodeElement uses xml:",innerxml" for raw CDATA injection
- `internal/codegen/validate.go` — validator public interface:
  - ErrorLayer enum (Structural, Referential, Semantic)
  - ValidationError struct (Layer, ElementPath, Message)
  - SchemaIndex struct (all ID sets + metadata)
  - func ValidateSchema(r io.Reader) ([]ValidationError, error)
  - func ValidateTree(root *etree.Element) []ValidationError (or encoding/xml parsed doc)

### Wave 2: Implementations (parallel, 3 workers)

**SLICE-B: Hybrid XML refactor** (depends on SLICE-A types)
- Refactor schema.go: replace 17 build* functions with struct population + xml.Marshal
- Keep manual CDATA injection only for <code> elements within constraints/procedure-steps
- Approach: populate AuraProtocol struct → xml.MarshalIndent → post-process CDATA placeholders
- CDATA strategy: use sentinel placeholder (e.g. `__CDATA_START__`/`__CDATA_END__`) in struct fields,
  then string-replace to `<![CDATA[`/`]]>` after marshalling (encoding/xml escapes CDATA otherwise)

**SLICE-C: 3-layer schema validator** (depends on SLICE-A interface)
- `internal/codegen/validate.go` — implementation:
  - Layer 1 (buildIndex): parse XML, extract all IDs, check required attrs, unique IDs
  - Layer 2 (checkRefs): all cross-refs resolve (phase-ref, role-ref, command-ref, etc.)
  - Layer 3 (checkSemantics): phase ordering, domain consistency, substep ordering, etc.
- Port all 14 semantic rules from Python validate_schema.py
- Uses encoding/xml or etree for XML parsing (NOT the spec structs — validates any schema.xml)
- Round-trip test: GenerateSchema → ValidateSchema → 0 errors

**SLICE-D: Enhanced test fixtures** (depends on SLICE-A types)
- Update testdata/skills.yaml: header-based assertions (must_contain_headers: ["## Constraints", "## Handoffs"])
- Update testdata/schema.yaml: constraints-based assertions (must_have_given_when_then per constraint)
- Update testdata/agents.yaml: figure-based assertions
- Add round-trip integration test: generate → validate → 0 errors
- Existing tests must continue to pass

### Wave 3: Integration (sequential)
- Verify all tests pass
- Run go generate and confirm schema.xml validates

## Key Design Decisions

1. **CDATA sentinel strategy**: encoding/xml cannot emit CDATA. Use placeholder strings in struct fields,
   post-process after MarshalIndent. This keeps struct marshalling clean while supporting CDATA.
2. **Validator parses XML independently**: The validator does NOT import the schema types — it parses
   arbitrary schema.xml files. This validates the actual output, not just the Go structs.
3. **encoding/xml vs etree**: For the validator, encoding/xml's streaming decoder (xml.Decoder) is
   sufficient for ID extraction and ref checking. No need for etree dependency.
4. **Test fixture enhancement is additive**: Existing must_contain assertions stay. New header-based/
   constraints-based assertions are added alongside.

## Acceptance Criteria

Given generated schema.xml when validated then 0 errors across all 3 layers should never have referential integrity violations
Given encoding/xml marshalling when generating non-CDATA sections then output matches current manual output should never break existing test assertions
Given CDATA code examples when marshalling then CDATA sections preserved raw should never HTML-escape code content
Given test fixtures when running skills tests then header-based structural assertions pass should never couple to exact formatting","status":"open","priority":1,"issue_type":"task","owner":"dayvidpham@gmail.com","created_at":"2026-03-13T13:31:49Z","created_by":"David Huu Pham","updated_at":"2026-03-13T13:31:49Z"}

## Specification

Wave 2 slice (parallel with SLICE-B/D). Ports validate_schema.py (769 lines) to Go. Depends on SLICE-A validate.go interface types.

### Architecture
- Parser: encoding/xml → XMLNode generic tree (NOT streaming decoder)
- Implement Iter(tag), Find(tag), FindAll(tag), Attr(name) helpers on *XMLNode
- Use xml.Unmarshal into XMLNode for full document parse

### 3 Validation Layers
Layer 1 — buildIndex(root *XMLNode) (SchemaIndex, []ValidationError):
  Parse tree, extract all IDs, check required attrs, unique IDs

Layer 2 — checkRefs(root *XMLNode, index SchemaIndex) []ValidationError:
  All cross-refs resolve (phase-ref, role-ref, command-ref, etc.)
  11 major reference types from Python implementation

Layer 3 — checkSemantics(root *XMLNode, index SchemaIndex) []ValidationError:
  Port 12 implemented semantic rules (numbered 1-6 and 9-14; rules 7-8 absent):
  1. Phase numbers sequential (contiguous 1..N)
  2. Phase domain consistency (hardcoded mapping)
  3. Each phase has >= 1 substep
  4. Substep order sequential within phase
  5. Parallel substeps must have parallel-group or instances
  6. Label value uniqueness
  9. Each role owns >= 1 phase
  10. Command with <phases> requires <file> child
  11. Review axis letters unique
  12. Startup sequence step orders sequential
  13. Agent template min-count <= max-count
  14. Domain enum values match phase domains

### Error Contract (PROPOSAL-4 Fix A2)
- io.Reader read failure → return (nil, error)
- XML parse failure → return ([]ValidationError{{Layer: Structural}}, nil)
- Violations → return ([]ValidationError{...}, nil)
- Valid → return (nil, nil)

### Hard Independence Constraint
- Validator MUST NOT import codegen schema types (schema_types.go)
- Only imports validate.go types (ErrorLayer, ValidationError, SchemaIndex, XMLNode)

- internal/codegen/validate.go (MODIFY — implement stubs from SLICE-A)

- [ ] All 12 semantic rules ported from Python
- [ ] 3 layers: structural, referential, semantic
- [ ] XMLNode tree helpers: Iter, Find, FindAll, Attr

- [ ] No imports from schema_types.go

## Problem Space

PROPOSAL-1 was rejected at UAT. The user said: 'What you have been incorrectly calling the header and the body should not just be blindly merged into one string, but instead the content should be organized logically and should flow harmoniously.'

The current split is not just a marker boundary problem — it is a content organization problem. The header template puts dry reference tables (phases, commands, constraints, handoffs) before operational guidance (workflows, behaviors, recipes). An agent reading a skill file gets lookup tables before understanding what it should actually DO.

**Axes:** content narrative flow, template unification, reading comprehension for agents

**Has-a relationships:**
- A SKILL.md HAS-A YAML frontmatter (above BEGIN), HAS-A generated region (BEGIN...END), HAS-A hand-authored section (after END)
- The generated region HAS identity, HAS operational guidance, HAS reference material

## Engineering Tradeoffs

| Option | Pros | Cons | Decision |
|--------|------|------|----------|
| A: Blind concatenation (PROPOSAL-1) | Simple pipeline change | Content disorganized, UAT rejected | REJECT |
| B: Single unified template, merged context type | One template, logical flow, clean render | Must merge two context types, larger template | **ACCEPT** |
| C: Two templates with ordering contract | Keep templates separate, pipeline orders them | Two templates with implicit ordering contract is fragile | REJECT |

## Approach: Single Unified Template (Option B)

### Design Principle: Narrative Flow

An agent reading a skill file should encounter content in this order:
1. **Who am I** — identity, ownership
2. **What should I do** — behaviors, operational guidance
3. **How do I do it** — workflows, recipes, procedures
4. **Where do I look things up** — reference tables

### Proposed Unified Template Section Order

```
--- YAML frontmatter ---            (outside BEGIN, template-owned)
# {Role} Agent                      (outside BEGIN, template-owned)

<!-- BEGIN GENERATED FROM aura schema -->

**Role:** `{id}` | **Phases owned:** ...

### Introduction
{introduction prose}

### What You Own
{ownership narrative}

### Role Behaviors (Given/When/Then/Should Not)
{role-level tactical behaviors from RoleSpec.Behaviors}
{body-level operational behaviors from SkillBody.Behaviors}

{preamble — e.g., link to PROCESS.md}

{body sections — operational prose as H2/H3}
  e.g., "Ride the Wave", "First Steps", "Exploration", etc.

{body recipes — bd command templates as H2}
  e.g., "Creating Vertical Slices", "Spawning Workers", etc.

### Workflows
{workflow stages with figures}

### Startup Sequence
{boot procedure steps}

### Completion Checklist
{quality gates}

### Inter-Agent Coordination
{bd coordination commands table}

### Review Axes
{reviewer-only: axis evaluation table}

## Protocol Reference

### Owned Phases
{phase table}

### Commands
{commands table}

### Constraints (Given/When/Then/Should Not)
{constraint details with examples}

### Handoffs
{handoff table}

<!-- END GENERATED FROM aura schema -->
```

### Step 1: Merge context types

Create a unified `skillContext` struct that combines `skillHeaderContext` and `skillBodyContext`:

```go
type skillContext struct {
    // Identity (from header)
    Role                 RoleSpec
    OwnedPhases          []protocol.PhaseId
    PhaseSlug            map[protocol.PhaseId]string
    SubSkills            []string
    Introduction         string
    OwnershipNarrative   string

    // Behaviors (merged)
    Behaviors            []BehaviorSpec     // from RoleSpec
    BodyBehaviors        []BehaviorSpec     // from SkillBody

    // Body content
    Preamble             string             // from SkillBody
    Sections             []ProseSection     // from SkillBody
    Recipes              []RecipeBlock      // from SkillBody

    // Workflows + procedures
    Workflows            []Workflow
    FiguresByWorkflow    map[string][]FigureSpec
    Steps                []ProcedureStep

    // Checklists + coordination
    Checklists           []Checklist
    CoordinationCommands []CoordinationCommand
    ReviewAxes           []ReviewAxisSpec

    // Reference tables
    PhasesDetail         []PhaseSpec
    Commands             []CommandSpec
    Constraints          []ConstraintSpec
    Handoffs             []HandoffSpec
}
```

### Step 2: Write unified template

Create `templates/skill.go.tmpl` that renders ALL content in the logical flow above. Delete `skill_header.go.tmpl` and `skill_body.go.tmpl`.

### Step 3: New render function

Replace `renderHeader` + `renderBody` with a single `renderSkill(roleID, figuresDir)` function that:
1. Builds the unified `skillContext` (merging role context + body data)
2. Executes `skill.go.tmpl`
3. Returns the complete generated block (BEGIN...END inclusive)

### Step 4: Simplify GenerateSkill

Remove the two-pass logic entirely. GenerateSkill becomes:
1. Read file
2. Init markers if needed
3. Call `renderSkill(roleID, figuresDir)`
4. Call `ReplaceMarkerRegion(content, rendered, true)`
5. Validate structure
6. Diff + write

### Step 5: Delete dead code

- Delete `ReplaceBodyRegion` from markers.go
- Delete `skillHeaderContext` and `skillBodyContext` types
- Delete `renderHeader`, `renderBody` functions
- Delete `skill_header.go.tmpl` and `skill_body.go.tmpl` templates

### Step 6: Sub-skill handling

Sub-skills (`skill_sub_figure.go.tmpl`) do NOT have body content today — they only have figures. The sub-skill template already produces BEGIN...END as one block. For sub-skills WITH a SkillBody entry, create an analogous `renderSubSkill(commandID, figuresDir)` that builds a simpler context. However, examining SkillBodySpecs, sub-skills with body entries are: supervisor-plan-tasks, supervisor-spawn-worker, impl-review. These need the same treatment.

For sub-skills, the unified template should be `templates/skill_sub.go.tmpl` that includes:
1. Command badge
2. Body sections + recipes (if SkillBody exists)
3. Figures

### Step 7: Update tests

- Delete `TestReplaceBodyRegion_*` (4 tests)
- Rewrite `TestTwoPass_HeaderRegionUnchangedByBodyPass` → `TestGenerateSkill_BodyInsideMarkers` — assert body content is between BEGIN/END
- Keep `TestTwoPass_NoBodySpec_HeaderOnly` → rename to `TestGenerateSkill_NoBody_HeaderOnly`
- Keep `TestGenerateSkill_BodyPreserved` — hand-authored content after END is still preserved
- `TestGenerateIdempotent` must pass after regeneration

### Step 8: Regenerate on-disk SKILL.md files and update docs

Run `go generate`. Update CONTRIBUTING.md.

| `internal/codegen/templates/skill.go.tmpl` | **NEW** — unified template with logical section ordering |
| `internal/codegen/templates/skill_sub.go.tmpl` | **NEW** — unified sub-skill template |

- [ ] `go test -race ./internal/codegen/...` passes
- [ ] `go generate ./internal/codegen/...` produces zero diff
- [ ] TestGenerateIdempotent passes
- [ ] YAML frontmatter stays above BEGIN marker

## Requirements

### FR1: Error Handling — Narrow Exception Scope
Replace bare `except Exception` in `EpochWorkflow.run()` with `except TransitionError`. Failed transitions must be recorded in the audit trail (transition_history) with error context. Mutation test exception specificity (SLICE-1 bare except) must also be addressed.
- Findings: aura-plugins-3xe, aura-plugins-6wg, aura-plugins-i2g, aura-plugins-295

### FR2: Constraint Completeness — Full 22 C-* Coverage
Expand `RuntimeConstraintChecker.check_all()` to aggregate all 22 C-* constraint checks defined in schema.xml. Each constraint must have a dedicated method. `check_severity_tree()` must enforce the POSITIVE case of C-severity-eager (p10 MUST have 3 severity groups eagerly). EpochState needs a `severity_groups` field to enable runtime enforcement.
- Findings: aura-plugins-yno, aura-plugins-jwb, aura-plugins-947, aura-plugins-bnr

### FR3: Type Safety Hardening — Strongly-Typed Enums Throughout
Change `EpochState.current_role` from `str` to `RoleId`. Document TYPE_CHECKING Protocol limitations (isinstance checks only method name presence, not full signature) in interfaces.py module docstring. Add test verifying `RuntimeConstraintChecker` satisfies `ConstraintValidatorInterface` Protocol.
- Findings: aura-plugins-tcn, aura-plugins-don, aura-plugins-ngd, aura-plugins-5zf

### FR4: Temporal Integration Testing — Sandbox End-to-End
Add `WorkflowEnvironment.start_time_skipping()` integration tests for EpochWorkflow. Decouple timestamp from `advance()` by passing timestamp as explicit parameter. Test actual Temporal signal delivery (advance_phase, submit_vote) in sandbox.
- Findings: aura-plugins-68o, aura-plugins-gdx, aura-plugins-o83

### FR5: MINOR Bundled Cleanup
Address all MINOR findings alongside their IMPORTANT siblings:
- Duplicated `_advance_to` helper → shared conftest.py fixture (aura-plugins-sk6, aura-plugins-0yd)
- `DataPart.data` and `ToolCall` dict fields → `dict[str, Any]` (aura-plugins-utj, aura-plugins-eqy)
- `FilePart.file_uri` → document A2A migration path (aura-plugins-7d2, aura-plugins-hls)
- `SA_EPOCH_ID` per-transition upsert → document or make defensive (aura-plugins-xui, aura-plugins-r8f)
- `check_blocker_gate` constraint_id naming (aura-plugins-dvi, aura-plugins-qqf)
- `_SAME_ACTOR` frozenset → module-level constant (aura-plugins-pxo)
- `AuditEvent.payload` str → typed pattern (aura-plugins-h7x)
- Test `__import__` inline → top-level import (aura-plugins-v1b)
- Test hardcoded constraint subset → full set verification (aura-plugins-8jy)
- `TransitionRecord` post-hoc mutation → pass timestamp into advance (aura-plugins-x36, aura-plugins-3m4)
- `EpochState.current_role` str→RoleId (aura-plugins-1ic, aura-plugins-4hu)
- `ToolCall` hashability test documentation (aura-plugins-4u1)

## Constraints
- C-backwards: Must not break existing 475 tests
- C-no-new-deps: No new pip packages — only stdlib + existing deps (temporalio, pytest, pytest-asyncio)
- C-python-only: All code in aura-plugins must be Python (R7 from original URD)

## Priorities (User-Stated)
1. All 4 IMPORTANT themes equally prioritized
2. MINOR findings bundled with their IMPORTANT siblings (same-slice, same-pass)
3. Full 22 C-* constraint coverage (not a subset)

## MVP Goals
- check_all() covers all 22 C-* constraints with dedicated methods
- EpochWorkflow.run() catches only TransitionError, records failures
- EpochState.current_role typed as RoleId
- WorkflowEnvironment sandbox tests for signal delivery
- All MINOR cleanup addressed alongside IMPORTANT siblings
- 475+ tests pass (existing + new)

## End-Vision Alignment
This follow-up closes the gap between v1 MVP and the URD (aura-plugins-umi) requirements for:
- Forensic auditability (FR1: failed transitions recorded)
- Complete constraint enforcement surface (FR2: all 22 C-*)
- Strongly-typed protocol invariants (FR3: no str leaks)
- Temporal workflow confidence (FR4: sandbox tests prove signal delivery)"}

VOTE: ACCEPT — Test strategy is comprehensive and well-grounded in existing project conventions. All 7 review focus areas are satisfied.

## Review Summary (Axis B — Test Quality)

### 1. Test Strategy Sufficiency

The 4 new test files (test_schema_parser.py, test_gen_schema.py, test_gen_skills.py, test_context_injection.py) plus extensions to test_schema_types_sync.py provide complete coverage mapped to all new modules. Each new module has a dedicated test file. The mapping is 1:1 with module boundaries (schema_parser ↔ test_schema_parser, gen_schema ↔ test_gen_schema, gen_skills ↔ test_gen_skills, context_injection ↔ test_context_injection). This aligns with the existing pattern (constraints.py ↔ test_constraints.py, state_machine.py ↔ test_state_machine.py). No module is untested.

ASSESSMENT: ADEQUATE.

### 2. Error Path Coverage

AC1a specifies 3+ error-path tests for SchemaParseError with named failure inputs: malformed XML (truncated), missing required sections (e.g. `<phases>`), and missing required attributes. SchemaParseError is defined as a proper exception class with a clear docstring. The validation checklist has a dedicated entry.

AC4a specifies three distinct marker edge cases for MarkerError: (1) missing END marker → raise, (2) missing both markers → generate full content (clean path), (3) reversed markers → raise. The "should not silently discard body on any boundary error" invariant is the correct safety clause. MarkerError is defined as a ValueError subclass.

Together these are 6+ named error scenarios across 2 error types. The mutation-based approach from test_validate_schema.py provides a strong conceptual model that test_schema_parser.py can follow (inject bad inputs, assert specific exception with correct type).

ASSESSMENT: ADEQUATE.

### 3. Round-Trip Test Design

AC3 specifies "field-by-field comparison" and the validation checklist says "(not count-only)". The existing test_schema_types_sync.py at lines 294-308 (TestConstraintSpecsMatchSchema.test_constraint_given_when_then_match_schema) already demonstrates the correct pattern: iterate schema elements, look up the Python spec by ID, and assert each field individually (given, when, then). This is the exact model for AC3.

The proposal names specific fields per entity type in AC3: ConstraintSpec.given/when/then/should_not, HandoffSpec.required_fields, SubstepSpec.startup_sequence. These are concrete anchors that prevent count-only assertions. The test_gen_schema round-trip direction is: types.py → gen_schema → parse_schema → field-level comparison, which is a true integration test of two new modules working together. The prior Round 2 review B (aura-plugins-qt1p) correctly identified that AC3 should cover should_not (missing from the existing test_schema_types_sync.py pattern) — and the proposal now includes it explicitly.

ASSESSMENT: ADEQUATE. The model is demonstrated in the existing codebase and the proposal correctly extends it.

### 4. Absence Testing

AC5a names concrete constraint IDs: C-worker-gates must NOT appear in get_role_context(SUPERVISOR); C-supervisor-no-impl must NOT appear in get_role_context(WORKER). AC6a: C-severity-eager must NOT appear in get_phase_context(P4_REVIEW); C-review-consensus must NOT appear in get_phase_context(P9_SLICE).

These are precise, falsifiable assertions against specific string identifiers. They test the SUT's output (the returned frozenset), not internal state. They follow the project's convention of asserting observable outcomes. The validation checklist has two dedicated entries ("get_role_context does NOT include irrelevant constraints", "get_phase_context does NOT include irrelevant constraints").

One observation: these absence tests rely on the static _ROLE_CONSTRAINTS and _PHASE_CONSTRAINTS dicts in context_injection.py being correctly populated. Since these dicts are hand-authored (not derived from schema.xml structurally), the tests need to be robust enough that they catch errors in that hand-authored data. The named constraint IDs (C-worker-gates, C-supervisor-no-impl) provide exactly the right anchors.

ASSESSMENT: ADEQUATE.

### 5. Regression Safety

AC7 states "all 554 existing tests pass" and AC11 (Temporal Isolation) states "all sandbox tests pass unchanged" with an explicit enumeration of the 6 Temporal-serialized types that must NOT be modified (EpochState, TransitionRecord, EpochInput, EpochResult, PhaseAdvanceSignal, ReviewVoteSignal). ### Temporal Compatibility

**No breaking changes to Temporal-serialized types.** The Temporal workflow (workflow.py) serializes:
- EpochState (contains PhaseId, RoleId, VoteType, SeverityLevel)
- TransitionRecord (contains PhaseId)
- EpochInput, EpochResult, PhaseAdvanceSignal, ReviewVoteSignal

None of these types are modified. New types (RoleSpec, CommandSpec, etc.) are NOT used by Temporal — they're for code generation and context injection only.

**HandoffSpec.content_level str→ContentLevel change:** This is safe because HandoffSpec is NOT serialized by Temporal. It's only used in constraints.py for validation and in types.py as a static definition. The test_schema_types_sync.py test will need updating.

### context_injection.py Integration Points

context_injection.py is a pure lookup module — no side effects, no Temporal dependency:
- Reads from PHASE_SPECS, CONSTRAINT_SPECS, HANDOFF_SPECS (existing), ROLE_SPECS, COMMAND_SPECS, LABEL_SPECS (new)
- Called at skill invocation time (not from Temporal workflow)
- Called at phase transition time for prompt enrichment (not from Temporal workflow)
- Static mappings for constraint→role and constraint→phase (not in schema.xml; derived from constraint given: text)
- Returns frozen RoleContext / PhaseContext dataclasses

### Temporal Compatibility

**No breaking changes to Temporal-serialized types.** The Temporal workflow (workflow.py) serializes:
- EpochState (contains PhaseId, RoleId, VoteType, SeverityLevel)
- TransitionRecord (contains PhaseId)
- EpochInput, EpochResult, PhaseAdvanceSignal, ReviewVoteSignal

None of these types are modified. New types (RoleSpec, CommandSpec, ConstraintContext, etc.) are NOT used by Temporal — they're for code generation and context injection only.

**HandoffSpec.content_level str→ContentLevel change:** This is safe because HandoffSpec is NOT serialized by Temporal. It's only used in constraints.py for validation and in types.py as a static definition.

### context_injection.py Integration Points

context_injection.py is a pure lookup module — no side effects, no Temporal dependency:
- Reads from PHASE_SPECS, CONSTRAINT_SPECS, HANDOFF_SPECS (existing), ROLE_SPECS, COMMAND_SPECS, LABEL_SPECS (new)
- Called at skill invocation time (not from Temporal workflow)
- Called at phase transition time for prompt enrichment (not from Temporal workflow)
- Static mappings for constraint→role and constraint→phase (Python is SoT; gen_schema.py exports as role-ref/phase-ref into schema.xml)
- Returns frozen RoleContext / PhaseContext dataclasses with ConstraintContext (typed when+then)

### Temporal Compatibility

**No breaking changes to Temporal-serialized types.** The Temporal workflow (workflow.py) serializes:
- EpochState (contains PhaseId, RoleId, VoteType, SeverityLevel)
- TransitionRecord (contains PhaseId)
- EpochInput, EpochResult, PhaseAdvanceSignal, ReviewVoteSignal

None of these types are modified. New types (RoleSpec, CommandSpec, etc.) are NOT used by Temporal — they're for code generation and context injection only.

**HandoffSpec.content_level str→ContentLevel change:** This is safe because HandoffSpec is NOT serialized by Temporal. It's only used in constraints.py for validation and in types.py as a static definition. The test_schema_types_sync.py test will need updating.

### context_injection.py Integration Points

context_injection.py is a pure lookup module — no side effects, no Temporal dependency:
- Reads from PHASE_SPECS, CONSTRAINT_SPECS, HANDOFF_SPECS (existing), ROLE_SPECS, COMMAND_SPECS, LABEL_SPECS (new)
- Called at skill invocation time (not from Temporal workflow)
- Called at phase transition time for prompt enrichment (not from Temporal workflow)
- Static mappings for constraint→role and constraint→phase (not in schema.xml; derived from constraint given: text)
- Returns frozen RoleContext / PhaseContext dataclasses

### Temporal Compatibility

**No breaking changes to Temporal-serialized types.** The Temporal workflow (workflow.py) serializes:
- EpochState (contains PhaseId, RoleId, VoteType, SeverityLevel)
- TransitionRecord (contains PhaseId)
- EpochInput, EpochResult, PhaseAdvanceSignal, ReviewVoteSignal

None of these types are modified. New types (RoleSpec, CommandSpec, ConstraintContext, etc.) are NOT used by Temporal — they're for code generation and context injection only.

**HandoffSpec.content_level str→ContentLevel change:** This is safe because HandoffSpec is NOT serialized by Temporal. It's only used in constraints.py for validation and in types.py as a static definition.

### context_injection.py Integration Points

context_injection.py is a pure lookup module — no side effects, no Temporal dependency:
- Reads from PHASE_SPECS, CONSTRAINT_SPECS, HANDOFF_SPECS (existing), ROLE_SPECS, COMMAND_SPECS, LABEL_SPECS (new)
- Called at skill invocation time (not from Temporal workflow)
- Called at phase transition time for prompt enrichment (not from Temporal workflow)
- Static mappings for constraint→role and constraint→phase (Python is SoT; gen_schema.py exports as role-ref/phase-ref into schema.xml)
- Returns frozen RoleContext / PhaseContext dataclasses with ConstraintContext (typed when+then)

## Problem Space

**Axes:** code generation (schema → code, code → schema), drift elimination (38 SKILL.md files × 1 schema.xml), runtime context injection (role-level + phase-level), source-of-truth inversion (schema.xml → Python types.py)

## Engineering Tradeoffs

| Decision | Choice | Rationale |
|----------|--------|-----------|
| Source of truth | Python types.py | User requirement. Directly usable at runtime. |
| Bootstrap | Hybrid codegen + manual polish (UAT-1) | gen_types.py generates draft; developer reviews and merges. Saves transcription, retains control. |
| Template engine | Jinja2 (dev-only dep) | Industry standard. StrictUndefined catches errors. |
| XML generation | xml.etree.ElementTree | Stdlib, no new dependency |
| SKILL.md split | Marker-based (markers required) (UAT-5) | gen_skills.py raises MarkerError if no markers found. No silent prepending. |
| ProcedureStep | Populated for supervisor+worker POC (UAT-6) | Proves the pattern end-to-end. Other roles deferred. |
| content_level typing | ContentLevel enum (from str) | Type safety; non-breaking (not Temporal-serialized) |
| Constraint→role mapping | Static dicts in Python → role-ref/phase-ref in XML (UAT-3) | Python is SoT; gen_schema.py exports structural attributes into schema.xml |
| Context injection types | ConstraintContext frozen dataclass (UAT-4) | Typed when+then fields, not bare strings. Strongly-typed throughout. |
| Generation diff output | gen_schema + gen_skills show diff (UAT-2) | User requirement: must see what changed on each generation run. |

### Temporal Compatibility

**No breaking changes to Temporal-serialized types.** The Temporal workflow (workflow.py) serializes:
- EpochState (contains PhaseId, RoleId, VoteType, SeverityLevel)
- TransitionRecord (contains PhaseId)
- EpochInput, EpochResult, PhaseAdvanceSignal, ReviewVoteSignal

None of these types are modified. New types (RoleSpec, CommandSpec, ConstraintContext, etc.) are NOT used by Temporal — they're for code generation and context injection only.

**HandoffSpec.content_level str→ContentLevel change:** This is safe because HandoffSpec is NOT serialized by Temporal. It's only used in constraints.py for validation and in types.py as a static definition.

### context_injection.py Integration Points

context_injection.py is a pure lookup module — no side effects, no Temporal dependency:
- Reads from PHASE_SPECS, CONSTRAINT_SPECS, HANDOFF_SPECS (existing), ROLE_SPECS, COMMAND_SPECS, LABEL_SPECS (new)
- Called at skill invocation time (not from Temporal workflow)
- Called at phase transition time for prompt enrichment (not from Temporal workflow)
- Static mappings for constraint→role and constraint→phase (Python is SoT; gen_schema.py exports as role-ref/phase-ref into schema.xml)
- Returns frozen RoleContext / PhaseContext dataclasses with ConstraintContext (typed when+then)

## Problem Space

**Axes:** code generation (schema → code, code → schema), drift elimination (38 SKILL.md files × 1 schema.xml), runtime context injection (role-level + phase-level), source-of-truth inversion (schema.xml → Python types.py)

## Engineering Tradeoffs

| Decision | Choice | Rationale |
|----------|--------|-----------|
| Source of truth | Python types.py | User requirement. Directly usable at runtime. |
| Bootstrap | Hybrid codegen + manual polish (UAT-1) | gen_types.py generates draft; developer reviews and merges. Saves transcription, retains control. |
| Template engine | Jinja2 (dev-only dep) | Industry standard. StrictUndefined catches errors. |
| XML generation | xml.etree.ElementTree | Stdlib, no new dependency |
| SKILL.md split | Marker-based (markers required) (UAT-5) | gen_skills.py raises MarkerError if no markers found. No silent prepending. |
| ProcedureStep | Populated for supervisor+worker POC (UAT-6) | Proves the pattern end-to-end. Other roles deferred. |
| content_level typing | ContentLevel enum (from str) | Type safety; non-breaking (not Temporal-serialized) |
| Constraint→role mapping | Static dicts in Python → role-ref/phase-ref in XML (UAT-3) | Python is SoT; gen_schema.py exports structural attributes into schema.xml |
| Context injection types | ConstraintContext frozen dataclass (UAT-4) | Typed when+then fields, not bare strings. Strongly-typed throughout. |
| Generation diff output | gen_schema + gen_skills show diff (UAT-2) | User requirement: must see what changed on each generation run. |

VOTE: ACCEPT — Test strategy is comprehensive and well-grounded in existing project conventions. All 7 review focus areas are satisfied.

## Review Summary (Axis B — Test Quality)

### 1. Test Strategy Sufficiency

The 4 new test files (test_schema_parser.py, test_gen_schema.py, test_gen_skills.py, test_context_injection.py) plus extensions to test_schema_types_sync.py provide complete coverage mapped to all new modules. Each new module has a dedicated test file. The mapping is 1:1 with module boundaries (schema_parser ↔ test_schema_parser, gen_schema ↔ test_gen_schema, gen_skills ↔ test_gen_skills, context_injection ↔ test_context_injection). This aligns with the existing pattern (constraints.py ↔ test_constraints.py, state_machine.py ↔ test_state_machine.py). No module is untested.

ASSESSMENT: ADEQUATE.

### 2. Error Path Coverage

AC1a specifies 3+ error-path tests for SchemaParseError with named failure inputs: malformed XML (truncated), missing required sections (e.g. `<phases>`), and missing required attributes. SchemaParseError is defined as a proper exception class with a clear docstring. The validation checklist has a dedicated entry.

AC4a specifies three distinct marker edge cases for MarkerError: (1) missing END marker → raise, (2) missing both markers → generate full content (clean path), (3) reversed markers → raise. The "should not silently discard body on any boundary error" invariant is the correct safety clause. MarkerError is defined as a ValueError subclass.

Together these are 6+ named error scenarios across 2 error types. The mutation-based approach from test_validate_schema.py provides a strong conceptual model that test_schema_parser.py can follow (inject bad inputs, assert specific exception with correct type).

ASSESSMENT: ADEQUATE.

### 3. Round-Trip Test Design

AC3 specifies "field-by-field comparison" and the validation checklist says "(not count-only)". The existing test_schema_types_sync.py at lines 294-308 (TestConstraintSpecsMatchSchema.test_constraint_given_when_then_match_schema) already demonstrates the correct pattern: iterate schema elements, look up the Python spec by ID, and assert each field individually (given, when, then). This is the exact model for AC3.

The proposal names specific fields per entity type in AC3: ConstraintSpec.given/when/then/should_not, HandoffSpec.required_fields, SubstepSpec.startup_sequence. These are concrete anchors that prevent count-only assertions. The test_gen_schema round-trip direction is: types.py → gen_schema → parse_schema → field-level comparison, which is a true integration test of two new modules working together. The prior Round 2 review B (aura-plugins-qt1p) correctly identified that AC3 should cover should_not (missing from the existing test_schema_types_sync.py pattern) — and the proposal now includes it explicitly.

ASSESSMENT: ADEQUATE. The model is demonstrated in the existing codebase and the proposal correctly extends it.

### 4. Absence Testing

AC5a names concrete constraint IDs: C-worker-gates must NOT appear in get_role_context(SUPERVISOR); C-supervisor-no-impl must NOT appear in get_role_context(WORKER). AC6a: C-severity-eager must NOT appear in get_phase_context(P4_REVIEW); C-review-consensus must NOT appear in get_phase_context(P9_SLICE).

These are precise, falsifiable assertions against specific string identifiers. They test the SUT's output (the returned frozenset), not internal state. They follow the project's convention of asserting observable outcomes. The validation checklist has two dedicated entries ("get_role_context does NOT include irrelevant constraints", "get_phase_context does NOT include irrelevant constraints").

One observation: these absence tests rely on the static _ROLE_CONSTRAINTS and _PHASE_CONSTRAINTS dicts in context_injection.py being correctly populated. Since these dicts are hand-authored (not derived from schema.xml structurally), the tests need to be robust enough that they catch errors in that hand-authored data. The named constraint IDs (C-worker-gates, C-supervisor-no-impl) provide exactly the right anchors.

ASSESSMENT: ADEQUATE.

### 5. Regression Safety

AC7 states "all 554 existing tests pass" and AC11 (Temporal Isolation) states "all sandbox tests pass unchanged" with an explicit enumeration of the 6 Temporal-serialized types that must NOT be modified (EpochState, TransitionRecord, EpochInput, EpochResult, PhaseAdvanceSignal, ReviewVoteSignal). The "unchanged" files list explicitly includes state_machine.py, constraints.py, workflow.py, interfaces.py — all of which have comprehensive existing tests (test_state_machine.py ~120, test_constraints.py ~180, test_workflow.py ~60, test_interfaces.py ~40).

The HandoffSpec.content_level str→ContentLevel change (the one non-additive modification) is correctly called out in the proposal as requiring test_schema_types_sync.py to update (line 346 comparison `spec.content_level == h.get("content-level")` will need to compare the enum value string, not the enum itself).

One specific gap: the proposal does not explicitly call out that test_schema_types_sync.py's TestHandoffSpecsMatchSchema.test_handoff_roles_match_schema will need updating for the content_level field after the str→ContentLevel change. This is a valid implementation concern but it is traceable from the validation checklist ("test_schema_types_sync.py covers all new canonical dicts") and the "modified files" table (test_schema_types_sync.py listed as modified). A worker reading both sections can connect the dots.

ASSESSMENT: ADEQUATE. The regression strategy is sound. The one gap (content_level comparison update) is traceable from proposal text.

### 6. Integration Test Coverage

AC10 specifies the end-to-end pipeline test: parse_schema → populate types → gen_schema → validate_schema → gen_skills. This exercises all 4 new modules in sequence plus the existing validate_schema.py. This is a true integration test — not a mock-based test — because it runs the actual parsing, generation, and validation logic. It follows the project's convention (test_validate_schema.py already tests validate_schema.py via both the library API and subprocess CLI).

The prior Round 2 Review B (aura-plugins-qt1p) noted the "pipeline direction ambiguity" in AC10 (bootstrap vs. steady-state) as an IMPORTANT finding. PROPOSAL-3 does not resolve this ambiguity — AC10 still reads "parse_schema → populate types → gen_schema → validate_schema → gen_skills" which mixes bootstrap (schema→Python) and steady-state (Python→schema) steps. The validation checklist uses the slightly different phrasing "parse → gen_schema → validate → gen_skills" which omits "populate types".

This is the same IMPORTANT finding from Round 2 — not a new BLOCKER. Workers can resolve it by reading both documents together, and the checklist phrasing is the more actionable guide. Both pipeline directions are valid to test.

ASSESSMENT: ADEQUATE for a plan-review vote. The ambiguity is pre-existing, documented, and not a blocker.

### 7. Existing Test Pattern Alignment

Reading conftest.py and test_schema_types_sync.py reveals the following conventions:
- Class-per-concern grouping (TestPhaseIdMatchesSchema, TestConstraintSpecsMatchSchema, etc.)
- Module-scoped fixtures for expensive resources (schema_root fixture with scope="module")
- Field-level assertions with informative error messages (f-string showing both sides)
- pytest.mark.parametrize for combinatorial coverage (mutation tests, template rendering across 4 roles)
- from __future__ import annotations at the top
- Absolute Path construction via Path(__file__).resolve().parent

The proposal's test design aligns well with these conventions:
- AC8 uses pytest.mark.parametrize over 4 role templates (aligns with TestMutationDetection pattern)
- AC3 round-trip uses field-level assertions (aligns with test_constraint_given_when_then_match_schema pattern)
- test_schema_parser.py error paths can use SchemaFixture-style mutation injection
- The module-scoped schema_root fixture from test_schema_types_sync.py should be shared or replicated in test_gen_schema.py — the proposal does not explicitly specify this, but it is implied by the existing pattern

One alignment gap: the proposal does not specify whether the new test files should use module-scoped fixtures for the parse_schema() call (expensive XML parse). This is a minor implementation detail the worker should follow from convention, not a plan-level concern.

ASSESSMENT: ADEQUATE. Proposal aligns with existing conventions.

## Verdict

All 7 review focus areas are satisfied. The test strategy is comprehensive, well-anchored in named failure inputs and named constraint IDs, field-level comparison is modelled on existing code, regression safety is explicitly scoped, and integration coverage exercises all 4 new modules end-to-end. No new blockers identified beyond the pre-existing AC10 direction ambiguity (already documented in prior Round 2 review as IMPORTANT, not BLOCKER).
